policies.policy_name: Role‑based permission to create Knowledge articles
policies.description: The user invoking **create_knowledge_article** must have a role that grants Full CRUD access to the **knowledge** table (Administrator, Manager, or Agent). Verify the caller’s role before calling the tool.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables.
Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables.

policies.description: Any request to create a record, including a Knowledge article, must include and validate all mandatory fields defined for the operation.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.policy_name: Knowledge article creation requires required parameters
policies.description: When creating a Knowledge article, the request must provide the required parameters **title** and **owner_id** as defined by the tool schema.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: Only knowledge articles whose state is set to **published** can be searched by users with the Reporter role.
references: Article Status: Only articles in knowledge.state = published are searchable by the Reporter role.

policies.description: When creating or updating a knowledge article, the **state** field must be one of the allowed enumeration values defined for the knowledge table.

policies.policy_name: Owner must be an active user
policies.description: When creating a Knowledge article, the **owner_id** must reference a user whose **users.active = true** status. The system must validate that the specified owner is an active user before invoking **create_knowledge_article**.
references: User Status: Ensure any user being assigned to (assigned_to) or updated is users.active = true.
